newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in quiet trading as a recent rise in domestic interest rates continued to put a premium on investment in the fixed-income market instead of equities.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up a miniscule 0.01 percent at 13,593.18 on trading volume of 1.09 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB slipped 0.22 percent, ending the week at 868.24 on 854 million pesos.
"The market was very apathetic," a Bogota-based broker said. He and others attributed the poor trading to rising interest rates, which add to the attraction of securities.
Brokers said the IBB slipped on profit-taking in several heavily-traded issues, including Banco de Colombia, which fell 0.69 percent to close at 429 pesos.

Blue-chip Banco Ganadero also ended lower for the second consecutive day, closing down 0.73 percent at 271 pesos per share. Cementos Argos, another victim of profit-taking, led the losers in Bogota by falling 1.81 percent to end at 5,400 pesos per share.
The day's few winners in Bogota included Banco de Bogota, which closed up 0.16 percent at 6,010 and brewer Bavaria SA, which ended up 0.75 percent at 4,000 pesos a share.
"There was good investor and foreign fund demand for Bavaria," one broker said.
Bavaria's gains were more limited in Medellin, where it closed up just 0.03 percent, also at 4,000 pesos per share.

Cementos del Valle was the day's most actively traded issue in Medellin, accounting for 598 million pesos of total volume. It closed up just 0.01 percent, however, ending the day at 4,109 pesos a share.
Colombian banks and financial markets will be closed Monday in observance of a national holiday.
